directors typically work on an average of 3.4 projects per year
with 78% of directors reporting that they find their income unstable

figures.finding: Across live-action fiction features released in US cinemas in 2000-2019, a first-time feature director was 40.0 years old on average, against 48.8 for repeat directors; debuts fell from 29.5% of releases in 2000 to 16.7% in 2018.
figures.applies: US theatrical releases, live-action fiction features, 2000-2019; age at the film's first public screening; prior shorts, TV or other directing not excluded.
figures.replaces: When a first feature comes: the game should centre a debut near age 40 for US theatrical releases, not in the twenties.

sources.said: Between 2000 and 2019, the average age of a first-time director was 40.0 years old, compared with 48.8 for repeat directors.
In 2000, there were 390 films released, of which 29.5% were by first-time directors, whereas in 2018 there were 480 films released, of which just 16.7% were directing debuts.
